chunks: And with the former chains of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Wasil ibn Sulaiman, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say:
The Messiah, peace be upon him, used to say to his disciples:

"If you are my beloved ones and my brothers, then prepare yourselves for enmity and hatred from people. If you do not do so, then you are not my brothers. I only teach you so that you may act upon it, not so that you may marvel at it. You will never attain what you desire except by abandoning what you crave and by being patient with what you dislike. Beware of the [lustful] glance, for it sows desire in the heart of its beholder, and that alone is enough temptation for him. Blessed is he who sees temptations with his eyes but does not commit sins with his heart.

How far is that which has passed! How near is that which is coming! Woe to those deluded by vanity, when that which they detest draws near, and that which they love departs, and that which they were warned of arrives. Indeed, in the creation of this night and day there is a lesson. Woe to the one whose entire concern is this world and whose deeds are all sins -- how will he be disgraced tomorrow before his Lord! And do not speak excessively about things other than the remembrance of God, for indeed those who speak excessively about things other than the remembrance of God have hardened hearts, but they do not know.

Do not look into the faults of people as though you were overseers over them; rather, look into the salvation of your own selves, for you are but owned slaves. For how long does water flow upon the mountain without softening it? For how long will you study wisdom without your hearts softening from it? Slaves of evil -- neither pious slaves nor noble free men. Your example is like that of the oleander: its flower pleases whoever sees it, but it kills whoever tastes it. And peace."

key_terms.الدفلى: Oleander (Nerium oleander) -- a poisonous flowering plant, used as a parable for deceptive beauty
key_terms.العداوة: Enmity, hostility -- the social cost of following the path of truth
key_terms.النظرة: The [lustful] glance -- looking with desire at what is forbidden
key_terms.معتبر: A lesson, something to reflect upon and draw moral insight from

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Isa (Jesus) say to his disciples about patience and worldly desires in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a sermon of Prophet Isa (Jesus, AS) to his disciples, delivered in the context of preparing them for the hostility they would face for following his path. Isa exhorts them to abandon worldly desires, guard against the lustful gaze, reflect on the transience of life, remember God constantly rather than engaging in idle talk, focus on self-purification rather than fault-finding in others, and let wisdom truly soften their hearts. He closes with the vivid parable of the oleander -- beautiful to behold but deadly to taste -- as a warning against outward appearance without inner substance.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 43. And with the former chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Wasil ibn Sulaiman, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say that Isa, peace be upon him, used to say to his disciples: "If you are my friends and my brothers, then prepare your minds to reconcile with all the hostility and hatred coming from people.

If you are not so mentally prepared, then you are not my brothers. I teach you so that you may learn; and I do not teach you to please you. You will not attain your goal till you renounce your desires and by forbearance over that which you hate. I warn you against the evil glance, for it sows the seeds of lust in the heart of the beholder; and that is enough to tempt him. Blessed is he who beholds with his two eyes the tempting love of lust, but does not allow his heart to err.

How far is that which one has missed; and how close is that which is to come! Woe unto those beguiled by vanity, should that which they loathe come to them too soon, and that which they love dearly depart, and that of which they had been warned arrive! Indeed, in the creation of these nights and days, there is a lesson. Woe unto him whose entire concern is about this world only, and whose deeds are all evil and sins. How will he stand exposed before his Sustainer tomorrow! And do not talk much about things other than remembering Allah! Surely, those who talk much other than remembering Allah, have their hearts hardened, but they do not know.

Do not engage yourselves in looking into other people’s shortcomings and faults, as if you were their spies; instead, look into ways of freeing yourselves; for surely you are possessed slaves. How often does water flow on the mountain, but it does not soften? For how long have you studied words of wisdom, but your hearts do not soften for them? Slaves of the evil people and not of the pious! Nor are you liberated men of honour! Your example is that of oleander whose flower pleases the beholder, but its taste kills - Peace be with you."
